A B S T R A C T
The microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of a Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic low-density steel at different
hot-rolling reductions have been investigated. It was found that with the increase in hot-rolling reduction from
45% to 82%, the grain size was uniformly refined and the dislocation density was continuously increased. As a
result, both yield strength and ultimate tensile strength were effectively enhanced while the ductility and
toughness only slightly decreased. An excellent combination of yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total
elongation, and toughness of 648 MPa, 976 MPa, 50%, and 105
\mathbf { J } / \mathbf { m } ^ { 2 } ;
, respectively, was obtained. The yield
strength increment was interpreted by the stronger grain boundary strengthening and dislocation strengthening,
and the minor loss of ductility and toughness was arising from the faster saturation of the slip band refinement
(slip band spacing reached ~50 nm) and an earlier occurrence of microbands due to the finer grain size. Based on
this research, it is proposed that increasing the hot-rolling reduction was an effective approach to enhance the
overall mechanical properties of the low-density steel with a fully austenitic microstructure

chemical composition of Fe-31Mn-9Al-1C-0.45Nb-0.45Mo-0.45 W was

2. Applied methods
2.1. Experimental
In the present study, the investigated Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel
possessed a nominal chemical composition of Fe-31Mn-9Al-1C-0.45Nb-
0.45Mo-0.45 W (wt%). The exact content of alloying elements (wt%)
was: Mn 30.9, Al 8.7, C 0.9, Nb 0.45, Mo 0.45, W 0.43, and Fe in balance.
The steel was fabricated using the high-frequency vacuum induction
melting furnace and then hot-forged into billets with a thickness of 110
mm at 1150 <sup>◦</sup>C and then air cooling to room temperature. The hot-forged
billets were initially reheated at 1150 <sup>◦</sup>C and then hot-rolled into plates
with thicknesses of 60 mm, 35 mm, and 20 mm (hot-rolling reduction:
45%, 68%, 82%), which were denoted as HR45, HR68, and HR82
samples, respectively, and then water quenching to room temperature.
The number of passes during hot rolling were 4, 6, and 9 for the HR45,
HR68, and HR82 samples. The density of the investigated steel is 6.82 g/
\mathrm { c m } ^ { 3 }
(measured using Archimedes’ principle). In comparison to pure
iron, a density reduction of ~13% was attained.

present steel increased continuously with increasing hot-rolling
reduction.

5. Conclusions
In the present study, an excellent combination of strength, ductility,
and toughness of a Fe-31Mn-9Al-0.9C-0.45Nb-0.45Mo-0.45 W (wt%)
austenitic low-density steel was obtained by increasing the hot-rolling
reduction from 45% to 82%. The contributions of different strength
ening mechanisms and the correlation between the evolution of the
deformation substructures and the strain-hardening behavior have been
systematically investigated for the samples at different hot-rolling re
ductions. The major conclusion can be drawn as follows:
1. With the increasing hot-rolling reduction from 45% to 82%, the
mean effective grain size including annealing twin boundaries was
refined from 21.82 μm to 7.02 μm thanks to the enhanced dynamic
recrystallization (DRX), which provided more nucleation sites during
hot deformation, and the residual dislocation density after hot rolling
increased from

due to the higher
unrelieved deformation energy, while the volume fraction of the
precipitates barely changed.
2. With the increase in the hot-rolling reduction, the mechanical
properties were enhanced from the hot-rolling reduction of 45% to
82% with yield strength and ultimate tensile strength increased from
MPa to 648.0 ± 13.0 MPa and 861.0 ± 11 MPa to 976.0

3. The improvement of yield strength was mainly ascribed to the
stronger strengthening effect from grain boundary strengthening and
dislocation strengthening. The remaining good ductility and tough

5. Conclusions
In the present study, an excellent combination of strength, ductility,
and toughness of a Fe-31Mn-9Al-0.9C-0.45Nb-0.45Mo-0.45 W (wt%)
austenitic low-density steel was obtained by increasing the hot-rolling
reduction from 45% to 82%. The contributions of different strength
ening mechanisms and the correlation between the evolution of the
deformation substructures and the strain-hardening behavior have been
systematically investigated for the samples at different hot-rolling re
ductions. The major conclusion can be drawn as follows:
1. With the increasing hot-rolling reduction from 45% to 82%, the
mean effective grain size including annealing twin boundaries was
refined from 21.82 μm to 7.02 μm thanks to the enhanced dynamic
recrystallization (DRX), which provided more nucleation sites during
hot deformation, and the residual dislocation density after hot rolling

3. The improvement of yield strength was mainly ascribed to the
